newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed lower on Friday, tracking drifting bund futures, but a new 10-year issue sparked lively domestic trade.

The finance ministry announced a tap issue of 5.75 percent bonds, maturity February 2007, catching some players who had been looking for a reopening of a current five-year issue on the hop, dealers said.
The extra supply in the longer end might help lure more money into the market, one said, as investors look to pick up yield. The steep curve has led to some extension already in the last few days.
Sales of the new issue starts Monday, but it was quoted around 100.45/53 in pre-trade, yielding around 5.69 percent, seven basis points below the equivalent Jan 2007 bund.

The amount of the issue will be determined by the tap sale and one analyst said the finance ministry might be tempted to try and move the whole 10 billion guilders generally seen as the critical mass for a benchmark issue in one tranche.
The issue sparked big volume at the longer end, with the current benchmark January 2006s trading heavily. The 2003 maturities were also in demand.
Government bond issuance is expected to be low this year.

The finance ministry said on Friday its capital market requirement in 1997 would drop by 14.35 billion guilders through a reduction in a cash balance previously held at the central bank. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
